items.followUp: Mention two precautions that help protect a computer user from phishing.

rubric.why: A user should avoid interacting with untrusted messages or links and check who sent them.
rubric.description: Avoid suspicious messages or verify the sender.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for advising the user to avoid suspicious links/emails or verify the sender's identity before responding.

rubric.why: Phishing attempts often try to obtain private information.
rubric.description: Do not disclose sensitive information; another valid safety measure may be given.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for advising against sharing passwords or other sensitive details, or for another valid precaution such as using security software.

modelAnswer: Do not open links or attachments in suspicious emails or messages; verify the sender before responding.
Never share passwords or other sensitive information through an untrusted website or message.

items.followUp: Name two common types of software piracy.

rubric.why: These are recognised forms of software piracy.
rubric.description: Name one valid type of software piracy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one correct type.

rubric.why: A second distinct type completes the response.
rubric.description: Name a second, different type of software piracy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for another correct type; do not award twice for the same type.

modelAnswer: Two types of software piracy are softlifting and hard-disk loading.

items.followUp: What is the purpose of FTP on a computer network?

rubric.why: FTP is the abbreviation for File Transfer Protocol.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying FTP as File Transfer Protocol.

rubric.why: FTP is used to transfer files between computers over a network.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that it is used to transfer, upload, or download files between computers over a network.

modelAnswer: FTP stands for File Transfer Protocol.
It is used to transfer files between computers over a network or the Internet.

items.followUp: Give one example of a hardware device that can be shared on a network and explain how it is shared.

rubric.why: Hardware sharing concerns physical computer equipment, such as a printer or storage device.
rubric.description: Identify hardware sharing as sharing a physical device.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a physical hardware device is shared, or for giving a valid example such as a printer.

rubric.why: A shared device can be accessed by more than one computer through a network.
rubric.description: Explain how sharing provides access to the device.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that networked computers can access or use the shared device.

modelAnswer: Hardware sharing is making a physical device, such as a printer, available to computers on a network.
This allows more than one computer to use the same device.

items.followUp: How many bits are in an IPv6 address, and how is it usually written?

rubric.description: State the length of an IPv6 address.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that an IPv6 address is 128 bits long.

rubric.why: IPv6 addresses are commonly represented as colon-separated groups of hexadecimal digits.
rubric.description: Describe the written form of an IPv6 address.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it is written in hexadecimal groups separated by colons.

modelAnswer: An IPv6 address is a 128-bit address.
It is usually written as eight groups of hexadecimal digits separated by colons.

items.followUp: What does a router do when it forwards a packet to another network?

rubric.why: A router uses destination information and its routing information to select a route.
rubric.description: Explain how the router selects a route.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning that it determines a suitable or best path using destination information or a routing table.

rubric.why: Routing forwards packets toward their destination across interconnected networks.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the router forwards the packet toward its destination or the next network.

modelAnswer: The router examines a packet's destination address and uses its routing table to select a suitable path.
It forwards the packet to the next network or router on the way to its destination.

items.followUp: Write an HTML tag that inserts an image into a webpage and state one benefit of using images.

rubric.why: The HTML img element, with a source specifying the image file, is used to add an image.
rubric.description: Explain how an image is added to a webpage.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the tag and its src attribute or otherwise explaining that the image file is specified.

rubric.why: Images can improve a page's appearance or communicate information visually.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid benefit, such as making the page attractive or illustrating information.

modelAnswer: An image is added to a webpage with the HTML tag, using its src attribute to specify the image file, for example: .
Images make a webpage more attractive and can help explain information visually.

items.followUp: Define an algorithm and give two ways it helps in solving a problem.

rubric.why: An algorithm is expressed as a sequence of instructions or steps.
rubric.description: Define an algorithm as a sequence of steps or instructions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing an algorithm as a step-by-step set or sequence of instructions.

rubric.why: An algorithm must have an end and be directed toward solving a problem.
rubric.description: Include the finite nature or problem-solving purpose of an algorithm.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that its steps solve a problem and/or that the process terminates.

rubric.why: An algorithm helps organise a solution and clarify the problem before coding.
rubric.description: Explain how an algorithm supports planning and understanding.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid role such as organising the solution in a logical order or helping to understand/break down the problem.

rubric.why: An algorithm can guide program development and make a solution easier to check or communicate.
rubric.description: Explain another practical benefit of an algorithm.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid benefit such as guiding coding, helping with testing/debugging, or being independent of a programming language.

modelAnswer: An algorithm is a finite, step-by-step sequence of clear instructions for solving a problem.
It organises the solution in a logical order and helps us understand and break down the problem.
It provides a plan that can be followed when writing a computer program.
An algorithm can be checked and corrected before coding, and it is independent of any particular programming language.
